title.narrative: Activity under preparation Integrated Solid Waste Management and Green Jobs in The Gambia

description.narrative: Solid waste management is crucial for The Gambia: it contributes to environmental preservation and sustainable urban development; and it impacts the tourism sector - one of The Gambia¿s largest economic pillars. The current waste management system faces multiple critical challenges, including informal dumping and burning, driven by rapid urbanization, changing consumption patterns, limited collection coverage, and inadequate treatment infrastructure. It results in environmental degradation, public health risks, and increased climate impacts (a large proportion of waste is burnt ¿ including plastic).The action has two main components. Component 1 intends to strengthen the waste systems and support green & circular economy in the Greater Banjul Area (which includes 58% of the total population of The Gambia), on activities with central Government and potentially twinning between European and local academic institutions. This component is complementary to the EU/EIB Global Gateway investment (360° approach) currently under discussion with the Government. Component 2 intends to strengthen the waste systems and support green & circular economy in selected secondary cities (growth centres). Both components will entail awareness raising on solid waste management; skills development (e.g. on collection, recycling, safety), capacity building to enhance planning capabilities, light infrastructure (e.g. fencing of dumpsites, recycling facilities, etc), provision of equipment (e.g. compactor trucks, tricycles, etc¿), supporting circular economy initiatives with the private sector.The action will be implemented as a Team Europe initiative (indirect management). Three Member States (Belgium, Spain and France) having expressed their interest to implement this initiative. A Team Europe approach is also meant to provide opportunities for the involvement of European companies.
